# Aim

Is the Illinois agility test time related to the age of young ice hockey
players? Times were measured with our video program (Python, `main.ipynb`)
for 20 children (8.8 to 17.7 years old).
Data: `results/measures_anonymous.csv` (anonymous ids P01 to P20).

# Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false

# Required packages (install once in the console):
# install.packages(c("ggplot2", "irr", "rmarkdown"))

library(ggplot2)   # graphics
library(irr)       # intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
```

# Data

```{r}
#| label: read-data

# Read the anonymous results produced by Python
# file.path() builds a path that works on Windows, Mac and Linux
data <- read.csv(file.path("results", "measures_anonymous.csv"))

# Structure of the table: column names and types
str(data)

# Number of children and check for missing values
cat("Number of children:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Missing ages:", sum(is.na(data$age_years)), "\n")
```

# Ranking of the children

```{r}
#| label: ranking-table

# Sort the children from the fastest (smallest time) to the slowest
data_rank <- data[order(data$time_video), c("id", "time_video")]
data_rank$rank <- seq_len(nrow(data_rank))

knitr::kable(data_rank[, c("rank", "id", "time_video")], digits = 3,
             col.names = c("Rank", "Child", "Time (s)"),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Illinois test: children ranked from fastest to slowest")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ranking
#| fig-cap: "Illinois test time of each child, from the fastest (top) to the slowest (bottom). Black line: median. Blue dashed line: 1st quartile (Q1). Red dashed line: 3rd quartile (Q3)."

# Colour: green = fastest, red = slowest, grey = others
data_rank$group <- "Other"
data_rank$group[1] <- "Fastest"
data_rank$group[nrow(data_rank)] <- "Slowest"

# Order of the bars: fastest at the top
data_rank$id <- factor(data_rank$id, levels = rev(data_rank$id))

# Quartiles of the times: Q1 (25%), median (50%), Q3 (75%)
q <- quantile(data_rank$time_video, probs = c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75))

ggplot(data_rank, aes(x = time_video, y = id, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = q[1], colour = "blue",  linetype = "dashed") +  # Q1
  geom_vline(xintercept = q[2], colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +      # median
  geom_vline(xintercept = q[3], colour = "red",   linetype = "dashed") +  # Q3
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f s", time_video)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Fastest = "forestgreen",
                               Slowest = "tomato",
                               Other   = "grey70")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, max(data_rank$time_video) * 1.12)) +
  labs(x = "Time (s)", y = "Child", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

# Values of the quartiles
cat("Q1:", round(q[1], 2), "s | Median:", round(q[2], 2), "s | Q3:", round(q[3], 2), "s\n")
```

# Time and age

## Description of the sample

```{r}
#| label: sample-description

cat("Age: from", min(data$age_years), "to", max(data$age_years), "years",
    "| median:", median(data$age_years), "years\n")
table(data$sex)
```

## Graph

```{r}
#| label: fig-age
#| fig-cap: "Illinois test time according to age. Line: linear regression with its 95% confidence interval."

ggplot(data, aes(x = age_years, y = time_video)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "black", fill = "grey80") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = sex), size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = id), vjust = -0.9, size = 2.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(F = "tomato", M = "steelblue")) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Illinois time (s)", colour = "Sex") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Correlation

```{r}
#| label: correlation

# Pearson correlation between age and time
cor.test(data$age_years, data$time_video, method = "pearson")
```

## Linear regression

```{r}
#| label: regression

# Model: time = intercept + slope * age
model <- lm(time_video ~ age_years, data = data)
summary(model)

cat("Each extra year of age changes the time by",
    round(coef(model)["age_years"], 3), "s\n")
```

## Checking the model (residuals)

A linear regression assumes that the residuals are normally distributed
and that their spread does not depend on the fitted values.

```{r}
#| label: fig-residuals
#| fig-cap: "Left: QQ plot of the residuals. Right: residuals against fitted values."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))   # two graphs side by side
qqnorm(residuals(model)); qqline(residuals(model), col = "red")
plot(fitted(model), residuals(model),
     xlab = "Fitted time (s)", ylab = "Residuals (s)")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: shapiro-residuals
shapiro.test(residuals(model))
```
